foehn.definition: A warm, dry downslope wind. In Jurançon it can interrupt the wet Atlantic pattern during the long autumn ripening season.
foehn.matters: It helps explain concentration and drying conditions without pretending the foothills are generally arid.

passerillage.definition: Concentration as grapes lose water and shrivel, usually while remaining on the vine in this Jurançon context.
passerillage.matters: It is a ripening and concentration path, not another word for botrytis.

sec.definition: Dry. In this appellation the word is part of the legal name Jurançon sec and corresponds to a maximum fermentable-sugar threshold.
sec.matters: A bottle labeled only Jurançon is not the dry category.

tries-successives.definition: Successive picking passes through the vineyard, selecting fruit as it reaches the intended maturity or concentration.
tries-successives.matters: The current rule requires this repeated selection for Jurançon other than the sec path.

vendanges-tardives.definition: Late harvest, used here as a regulated Jurançon mention with its own grape, harvest-date and sugar requirements.
vendanges-tardives.matters: It is a narrower legal path than simply harvesting ripe fruit late.

place:bearn.hero_kicker: Western Pyrenean foothills · ripeness without surrender
place:bearn.thesis: Here, ripeness is not the opposite of freshness. Rain-heavy Atlantic foothills, a drying autumn {{term:foehn|foehn}} and late, thick-skinned local grapes let growers choose dry, sweet or late-harvest paths without giving up acidity.

hero_facts.note: association scope · not total AOP area

place_story.kicker: The map is part of the lesson
place_story.text: Béarn is the cultural foothill world; Béarn AOP and Jurançon are legal wine areas. The active outlines keep those meanings separate and deliberately prioritize Jurançon when its shape overlaps the broader Béarn layer.
place_story.title: A cultural world is not an appellation polygon

place.lede: Read the physical problem first: a wet oceanic climate, steep foothill slopes and a warm drying wind during a long autumn.

grapes.intro: Two principal grapes · several local companions
grapes.lede: Petit and Gros Manseng are separate cultivars, not size grades. The accessory grapes matter too—and Raffiat de Moncade belongs to the wider Béarn vocabulary without entering the current Jurançon list.

people.lede: These producers are not a ranking. Together they make terraces, local grapes, dry-to-sweet range and estate scale concrete.

culture.lede: Jurançon culture is bigger than sweetness: patient harvest work sits beside a living French–Basque network of farming, mentorship and collaboration.

rules.lede: The rulebook clarifies what the landscape alone cannot: label words, grape roles, picking passes and fermentable-sugar thresholds.

grape_cards.copy: Tiny berries can accumulate sugar while holding unusually high acidity. That capacity supports several wine paths; it does not make every Petit Manseng sweet.
A distinct, vigorous Pyrenean cultivar with fruit that can stay on the vine for sweet wine—and a major working role in dry blends.
A distinct accessory variety. Its Bizkaia legal-name connection is useful border literacy, not permission to collapse it into Courbu.
Courbu is separately named in the Jurançon accessory list. It is not a long form of Petit Courbu.
A useful wider Béarn and Pyrenean rabbit hole, but not one of the varieties permitted by the current Jurançon specification.

lenses.text: The insider cue is not a flavor note. It is the work pattern: long autumn exposure, hand harvest, repeated passes and {{term:passerillage|passerillage}} where the fruit and rules call for it.
lenses.title: Patience is a farming verb

lenses.text: Imanol Garay and Alfredo Egia make the French–Basque edge visible as a network of work, mentorship and collaboration. Their relevance is cultural; it does not relocate their vineyards into Jurançon.
lenses.title: The border is a working network

groups.label: Core map distinction
groups.note: Jurançon and Béarn AOP can overlap. A map click prioritizes the more specific Jurançon lesson while keeping both records visible.

groups.label: Useful neighboring comparisons
groups.note: Nearby Manseng and western-Pyrenean routes that clarify what Jurançon shares—and what remains locally specific.

rules.intro: Jurançon’s legal names describe wine paths, not separate landscapes. {{term:sec|Sec}}, unqualified Jurançon and {{term:vendanges-tardives|vendanges tardives}} sit inside one geographic production area with different thresholds and harvest conditions.

featured_connections.reason: One map area becomes three clearly named white-wine paths.
Tiny berries, high acid retention and an unexpected genetic route back toward Jura.
A terrace estate where place, grape mix and production scope stay visible.

grape:petit-manseng.hero_kicker: A grape with sugar capacity—not a sweetness guarantee
grape:petit-manseng.thesis: Petit Manseng’s tiny berries can hold very high acidity while concentrating sugar. The grape creates possibility; the harvest and fermentation path decide whether the bottle says {{term:sec|sec}}, Jurançon or {{term:vendanges-tardives|vendanges tardives}}.

style_paths.name: Jurançon {{term:sec|sec}}
style_paths.note: Dry is a legal path with a maximum fermentable-sugar threshold—not evidence that Gros Manseng did all the work.

style_paths.name: Jurançon
style_paths.note: Sweet wine from the same geography, with hand harvest and successive picking passes shaping the route.

style_paths.name: {{term:vendanges-tardives|Vendanges tardives}}
style_paths.note: A narrower Manseng-only late-harvest mention with a later date and higher sugar floor.

affinities.reason: A documented close genetic relationship, carefully bounded short of parentage.
A separate Manseng cultivar sharing the principal legal role, not the large-berry version of the same grape.
An accessory local grape that sharpens the difference between a regional mix and a two-grape monoculture.

featured_connections.reason: The legal map where this grape can take dry, sweet and late-harvest paths.
A real genetic bridge to Savagnin without inventing parentage.
See Petit Manseng inside a four-grape terrace estate rather than as an isolated varietal idea.

producer:camin-larredya.hero_kicker: Jurançon · terraces and a four-grape estate mix
producer:camin-larredya.thesis: Camin Larredya makes scope visible: a 9.5-hectare certified-organic estate, four hectares of terraces, a local four-grape mix—and separately identified purchased fruit rather than one blurred domaine story.

producer:domaine-cauhape.hero_kicker: Monein · slope, altitude and stylistic range
producer:domaine-cauhape.thesis: Domaine Cauhapé is a scale-and-range anchor: southeast-facing Monein slopes rising toward 400 metres, with dry and sweet wines held in the same estate frame.

producer:clos-uroulat.thesis: Clos Uroulat’s current visitor range makes a useful correction: Jurançon can be read across dry, tender and sweet positions instead of as a single binary switch.

producer:domaine-de-souch.hero_kicker: Laroin · small scale and patient work
producer:domaine-de-souch.thesis: Domaine de Souch brings the world down to human scale: seven hectares, three local grapes, organic farming, biodynamic principles and manual harvest.
